title: Wi-Fi and device reachability troubleshooting
summary: Diagnose boot, station connection, AP fallback, IP, isolation, and OTA reachability.
body:
Device does not appear

  1. Capture Serial Monitor from reset.
  2. Check SSID/password and network band.
  3. Look for the configured fallback AP.
  4. Confirm DHCP address; static IP must match subnet/gateway.
  5. Disable phone mobile data or VPN temporarily if it diverts local traffic.

Web works but OTA is unreachable

Open the exact IP from the same phone/PC. Check guest/client isolation, VLANs, VPN, firewall, authentication, and address changes. Discovery failure does not prove direct-IP failure.

Unstable connection

Check RSSI, antenna placement, power, transmit power, and memory. Motor/audio noise can reset or disconnect the ESP; test with the load supply disconnected.

title: MQTT troubleshooting
summary: Diagnose cycling, authentication, duplicate clients, topics, commands, and discovery.
body:
Connection fails or cycles

  • Verify broker host/port from the same network.
  • Check credentials and ACLs.
  • Use a unique client ID; firmware adds a MAC suffix, but broker policies can still conflict.
  • Inspect disconnect reasons and reset/memory logs.
  • Remove accidental spaces from base topic.

Publish works, command does not

Use the exact compiled topic and payload. Subscriptions are absent when their feature is not compiled. A retained command can execute after reconnect; clear dangerous retained commands.

Discovery missing

Enable discovery, reconnect or republish, and confirm the feature has a runtime implementation. Configuration-only profiles do not create entities.

State does not update

MQTT Publish Out means queued, not acknowledged. Subscribe independently, inspect logs, and check the corresponding state topic.

title: Sensors, relays, ADC, I2C, and motors troubleshooting
summary: Diagnose common physical and configuration failures safely.
body:
Sensor zero, unavailable, or jumping

Confirm runtime support first. Check supply, ground, GPIO, pull resistor, ADC range, address, and cable length. Average noisy ADC values; never exceed input voltage.

Relay backwards or chatters

Determine active-high/low with the load disconnected. Chatter can come from one-threshold control, power noise, floating input, or repeated Flow. Use hysteresis and only the timing block whose documented behavior fits.

I2C not detected

Check SDA/SCL, address, pull-ups, voltage, and conflicts. Test one device before sharing the bus.

Motor does not move or resets ESP

Check motor supply, common ground, both direction pins, driver fault, and stall current. Separate motor paths and add recommended decoupling. Remove power if the driver gets hot.

Configuration rejected

Read the first validation message. Reserved pins, duplicates, unsuitable ADC, incomplete I2S, unsupported adapters, and graph limits are deliberate blockers.
